title: What do your parents do?
grammar: Present simple: third person (he works, she teaches)
pair_game: Point at a picture. Say: “He works in a …”. Your partner says the job. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: He works / She teaches
grammar_box.tip: Add -s for he, she, it: works, drives, helps. After ch/sh/s add -es: teaches, washes.

questions: Do your parents work every day?
Is your mom at home right now?
What time do your parents come home from work?
Do you want to do the same job as your parents?
What job do you think is interesting?
Tell me about your parents' jobs.
starters: My father is a … . He works in … .
My mother is a … . She works in … .
Yes, they work … days a week. / No, they do not work on … .
Yes, she is at home. / No, she is at … right now.
Yes, I want to be a … like my … . / No, I want to be a … .
Yes, they are very busy today. / No, they are free.
My mother is a … and my father is a … . They both … .
samples: My mother is a nurse. She **works** in a hospital and she **helps** children every day.
Do you want to do the same job as your parents?
No, I do not. My father **drives** a bus, but I want to be an engineer because I like maths.
Tell me about your parents' jobs.
My mother **teaches** maths at School 22. My father **works** in a big shop in the centre. He **starts** at nine and **finishes** at seven.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: What does somebody in your family do?

game.title: Find someone whose…
game.rules: Walk around the class. Ask: “Does your … work in a …?” Write a name.
items: … family member works in a hospital.
… relative has the same job as their parent.

mini_talk.title: Jobs in my family
mini_talk.model: My mother is a teacher. She **teaches** maths at School 22 and she **works** six days a week. My father is a shop assistant. He **works** in a big shop in the centre of our city. He **starts** at nine o'clock and **finishes** at seven. They are both very busy, but on Sundays we are all at home together. I want to be a doctor, because I like helping people.
